name: RSNA Pneumonia Detection 2018 — OCI Mirror
description: Curated re-publication of the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge dataset (2018) covering 30 000+ frontal chest radiographs (DICOM) with bounding-box annotations for lung opacities consistent with pneumonia. Mirrored into OCI Platform as the reference PUBLIC fixture: anyone may download the manifest and the upstream challenge bundle without a formal access request. Includes RSNA's labelling protocol, demographic skew, known biases, and licence terms reproduced verbatim from the original Kaggle release.

prov:wasAttributedTo.name: RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge — Radiological Society of North America
U.S. National Institutes of Health Clinical Center (source images)

rai:dataCollection: Source images come from the NIH Clinical Center ChestX-ray8 dataset (~112 000 frontal chest radiographs from ~30 000 unique patients, retrospectively curated 1992-2015 from the NIH PACS). RSNA filtered to 30 000 frontal images and re-annotated them for the 2018 challenge.
rai:dataCollectionType: Retrospective multi-site PACS extraction (NIH Clinical Center).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Eighteen board-certified radiologists annotated each image with bounding boxes around regions of opacity consistent with pneumonia. Each image was reviewed by at least three radiologists; final box was the majority-vote intersection. Three-way classification ('Normal', 'Lung Opacity', 'No Lung Opacity / Not Normal') was assigned post-annotation by a fourth thoracic radiologist.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Eighteen US-based board-certified radiologists, mix of academic and community practice; sub-specialty: thoracic radiology.
rai:dataBiases: Source cohort is a single US tertiary-care PACS (NIH Clinical Center) — patient population skews adult, with referral bias toward complex disease. Imaging protocols and equipment vendors reflect a single institution. Class imbalance: only ~6 000 of 30 000 images positive for opacity. Pneumonia label is a radiographic surrogate; ground-truth microbiological confirmation is not available.
rai:dataLimitations: Bounding boxes localise the opacity, not the underlying pathology — overlap with effusion, atelectasis, oedema is expected. No lateral views; frontal AP/PA only. No paediatric subjects. Image preprocessing (windowing, resampling) was not standardised in the public release.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: DICOMs were de-identified (HIPAA Safe Harbor) by NIH prior to public release; no direct identifiers remain. Date metadata shifted by per-patient random offset. No participant re-identification has been reported.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking pneumonia-detection classifiers and lung-opacity localisation models. Used as a teaching dataset for radiology AI curricula. Frequently combined with NIH ChestX-ray14 for transfer-learning experiments.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Held by RSNA in perpetuity via Kaggle. No further label updates are expected. RSNA AI Image Challenge programme committed to keeping the bundle online with stable URLs.
bio:dataAcquisitionProtocol: Frontal AP/PA chest radiographs acquired on a mix of computed-radiography and direct-digital-radiography systems used in routine clinical practice at the NIH Clinical Center 1992-2015. Images stored as 1024×1024 PNG-encoded 8-bit grayscale in the public release; original DICOM windowing not preserved.

bio:irbApproval.approvingBody: U.S. National Institutes of Health — Office of Human Subjects Research

bio:consentNotes: Waiver of informed consent granted by the NIH IRB for retrospective use of fully de-identified imaging data. RSNA's secondary annotation of the public set required no additional consent.
